result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.simrank_star_similarity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute SimRank* similarity between all node pairs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11162-L11245){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.simrank_star_similarity( importance_factor=0.8, max_iterations=100, tolerance=1e-06, method="closed_form", return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![SimRank* similarity](/assets/graphs/simrank-star-similarity.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Nodes B and E are outlined in the accent color, with shared neighbors C and D in accent. A 4 by 4 table, part of the full all-pairs result, gives SimRank* scores for B, C, D, and E with 1 on the diagonal; the highlighted B, E cells read 0.36." width="100%"} SimRank* fixes the "zero-similarity problem" of the original SimRank, where most node pairs receive a score of 0.0 on real-world graphs, by considering asymmetric in-link paths. The result is a similarity matrix where each entry `s(a, b)` is in `[0, 1]`, with `s(a, a) = 1.0`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [importance_factor]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.8]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Decay factor `C` in `[0, 1)`. Higher values propagate similarity further through the graph. Default is `0.8`. [max_iterations]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum iterations for the `"iterative"` solver. Ignored by `"closed_form"`. [tolerance]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence threshold for the `"iterative"` solver. Ignored by `"closed_form"`. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["closed_form"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : `"closed_form"` (default) solves the PJsim Lyapunov equation exactly in *O(n³)* time via Bartels-Stewart (real Schur decomposition). `"iterative"` uses fixed-point iteration in *O(K·n³)* time. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the raw nested dict `{node_a: {node_b: sim}}`. If `False` (default), store the similarity values as a node attribute and return the graph for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict, Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=True`, a nested dict of similarities. Otherwise, the graph with a `"simrank_star"` node attribute set to each node's similarity dict. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#d3814888 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True) for i in range(1, 5): g.add_node(label=str(i)) g.add_edge("1", "2").add_edge("1", "3") g.add_edge("2", "4").add_edge("3", "4") g.simrank_star_similarity(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {3: {3: 1.0, 1: 0.3563748119253343, 4: 0.19245008972987526, 2: 0.07407407407407407}, 1: {3: 0.3563748119253343, 1: 1.0, 4: 0.11946953821789978, 2: 0.3563748119253344}, 4: {3: 0.19245008972987526, 1: 0.11946953821789978, 4: 1.0, 2: 0.19245008972987526}, 2: {3: 0.07407407407407407, 1: 0.3563748119253344, 4: 0.19245008972987526, 2: 1.0}} ``` ::: :::
